vectors.description: PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY with no parameters. The message has no Request ID field: it is identified by the subscription's bidirectional stream it arrives on, like SUBSCRIBE_OK, PUBLISH_DONE and FETCH_OK

PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY carrying LARGEST_OBJECT (group=10, object=3). The publisher MUST include this parameter if known so the subscriber can locate the point in the Track at which the change took effect. LARGEST_OBJECT is Parameter Type 0x09 — odd, but a Location, i.e. two bare vi64s with no length prefix; the Key-Value-Pair odd/even rule does not apply to Message Parameters
PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY reporting that the Forwarding State now in effect at the publisher is 0
PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY reporting the Location Filter now in effect at the publisher: the inclusive range {12,0} through all of group 16
PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY carrying LARGEST_OBJECT (group=7, object=41) and FORWARD=1; demonstrates type-delta ordering (0x09 then a delta of 7 to 0x10)
PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY carrying every parameter draft-20 permits in it: LARGEST_OBJECT (0x09), FORWARD (0x10) and LOCATION_FILTER (0x21)

PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY carrying EXPIRES (0x08). Section 10.10 says "The semantics of each parameter, including whether it may appear in PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY, are defined by the parameter", and only LARGEST_OBJECT (0x09), FORWARD (0x10) and LOCATION_FILTER (0x21) name it. This corpus treats that list as closed, so anything else is a Section 10.2.1 PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. The draft implies the closure but never states it
vectors.error_detail: EXPIRES may appear in SUBSCRIBE_OK, PUBLISH, PUBLISH_OK, SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE_OK, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS_OK, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE_OK or REQUEST_UPDATE_OK; PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY is none of those

vectors.description: PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY carrying SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY (0x20). It is a subscription parameter, but a subscriber-controlled one, and its definition names SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, FETCH and REQUEST_UPDATE only. Section 10.10 says "The semantics of each parameter, including whether it may appear in PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY, are defined by the parameter", and only LARGEST_OBJECT (0x09), FORWARD (0x10) and LOCATION_FILTER (0x21) name it. This corpus treats that list as closed, so anything else is a Section 10.2.1 PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. The draft implies the closure but never states it
